title: The Encore Nobody Asked For
skyStory: The moon is still almost completely full, ninety-eight percent, and still in Leo, which means it has come back out for an encore nobody requested. It bows. It bows again. It tosses a rose made of starlight into the audience. Saturn checks his watch. Mars throws the rose back. The moon catches it, delighted, and bows a third time.

reading: Morning check: the onyx spent the night in the moonlight, and it looks exactly the same. That is how you know it worked. Put it on your right wrist, the giving side, and send a little of last night's glow over to the shore. Leave it there until lunch.

Leo wants you to perform today, so do something mildly theatrical. Read a recipe aloud like a dramatic monologue. Narrate the shovelling like a sports broadcast. Bow when somebody thanks you. [[The Fool]] is cheering from the front row in a paper crown. Nobody minds. It is Saturday.
joel.mission: Perform one ordinary task today as a full theatrical production, complete with a bow at the end.
joel.omen: Snow sparkling in the sun like stage glitter. It means your efforts are being noticed by the right audience.

reading: Your stones slept in the moonlight and are freshly charged. Put them back on one at a time, slowly, like a superhero suiting up. Pearl for water, diamonds for wind, ruby for fire and heart at once, onyx for earth. You are now fully elemental and slightly glowing.

Today Leo hands you a spotlight, and someone will ask you for a story, probably around 3:30 pm. Your hands will start before your mouth does. Let them. The [[Queen of Wands]] waits in the wings, nodding, holding a cat. Somebody will remember this story for years.
nancy.mission: Put your recharged stones back on one at a time, naming the element of each, out loud.
nancy.omen: A sunbeam landing exactly where you are sitting. It means the spotlight is yours today, so take it.

together.text: Leo is still in the room, so each of you sends the other a voice message introducing yourself like a headliner at a sold-out show. Full announcer voice. Fake crowd noise encouraged. The moon will be in the front row, still holding that starlight rose.
